milestones.name: On the CPU alone, rain fills the hollows of a stretch of ground: puddles stand level where it dips, spill into each other, join into one and part again as they dry, and ground under a roof stays dry
milestones.quality_bar: Standing water a hydrologist would accept, held to brute force as Barnes's fill-spill-merge is held to a flood: every puddle level in its own hollow, and every litre accounted for through each spill, merge and parting. Nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: `thrum-rain-model` cuts a bed grid into its tree of hollows. On a bed the test makes, with three bowls, a rut, a slope and small relief: every pit is a hollow; each cell is reached from its hollow's pit by a path that never descends; each pair's sill is the lowest pass between them; a hollow shallower than the profile's least depth is filled; a hollow under four cells across is reported; and the same bed gives the same bytes.
items.ask: Read the test. Are the expected hollows, sills and paths worked out there from the bed by brute force, without the code under test?

items.statement: The point test is exact. Over 200 seeded beds and fills, the cells where a hollow's level stands above the cell's bed are the cells a flood from the pits reaches under the same levels: no cell differs, with puddles that span one hollow and several.
items.ask: Is the flood in the test written apart from the tree's code, and does it start from pits only? Would a point test that read one level for the whole body fail it?

items.statement: Puddles fill, spill, merge and part. Under steady rain a full hollow's excess goes to the hollow across its sill; two that are full to one sill become one puddle at one level; under a loss they part at the sill, each keeping its own side's water. A hollow beyond a ridge stays dry until water spills into it. In every tick, a merge's and a parting's included, a hollow's level moves by no more than the water that entered or left its puddle's hollows in that tick over the smallest water surface any of those puddles had before or after it, taken as at least one cell.
items.ask: Does the test take its bound on a level's change from the tick's own volumes and surfaces, and does it cover a merge of two puddles that are each already several hollows? Would a fill that set both levels to their mean at a merge fail it?

items.statement: The water account closes. Over 10,000 ticks with merges and partings, the rain on the body equals the change in the puddles plus what dried, soaked, was withheld by canopy and left over the edge, within 1e-9 of the rain. A pothole with six times its area draining to it fills in a sixth of the time; on ground that soaks faster than the rain no puddle forms.

Shelter is content. From triangles the test gives, each with the share of rain it lets through, exposure is 0 under a roof, the crown's share under a tree, 1 under open sky, on the roof's own top and outside the grid, and passes between them over the profile's edge width. A hollow under a roof fills only by what drains to it from open ground, and one with no open ground stays dry.

Ruling 1 is built on the CPU: `thrum-water-model`'s map takes a hollows body (a rectangle, its own bed, a label for each cell, a level for each hollow) and gives the body, level, bed and depth at any point by the point test, with no current and no wind gain. Its identity and generation are the same before and after its puddles merge. Refused by name: a hollows body with a cell in another body's water or shore margin anywhere in that body's stage range, and one over the profile's count of cells or hollows. A table that stands two levels in wet cells that touch is held at the last table and counted.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model --test map && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Is the change to the map confined to the new kind, so that no body an existing test or the example declares is prepared or answered differently? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` changed?

items.statement: The rain state is plain data a game keeps in its world. It encodes and decodes to the same bytes, and stepping it from the same state and inputs gives the same bytes on one thread and on eight.

`WATERS`' conformance model answers on a hollows body: a point in a puddle gives the body and its depth, a point on dry ground between two puddles gives dry, and the answers either side of a merge differ only by the level's change.

`scripts/rain_cost.py` records, on this Mac in a release build, the preparation of a bed of 640,000 cells (seconds, hollows, nodes, bytes) and a fill step with every hollow holding water, with the commit and the load on the machine. `check` fails only when either cannot be measured or the committed record lacks a field.
items.ask: Was the record taken on this milestone's code, in a release build, and does it give the bytes a node's curve of level for volume takes?

items.statement: `thrum-rain-model` builds and its tests run with no graphics device and no dependency on `thrum-render` or `wgpu`, it is registered in `.config/architecture.toml`, and it holds no island, yard, preset or ground table.
items.check: cargo tree --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model -e normal | python3 -c 'import sys; t=sys.stdin.read(); sys.exit(1 if ("wgpu" in t or "thrum-render" in t or not t.strip()) else 0)'

milestones.name: On the CPU alone, ground wets and dries as ground does, sheen first and darkness last, and a raindrop's rings spread as water's own waves do
milestones.quality_bar: Wet ground and rain rings a physics text would accept: two stores that keep their water, darkening that follows from the film's optics, and rings that follow from water's dispersion, each held to the test's own arithmetic as part 3 to 6 of the design proof hold them.

items.statement: The ground's two stores step with the tick for each ground class, in the open and where a half and a quarter of the rain reaches. Through a shower on paving the pores fill, then surface water stands up to what the relief holds and the rest is runoff; after it the surface water goes at the drying rate and the pores' fill falls only once it has gone. Ground whose pores drink faster than the rain takes no surface water. With the stores in it, M1.4's account still closes within 1e-9.
items.ask: Are the expected times and fills worked out in the test from the rates, as part 5 of `docs/evidence/PUDDLES/design-proof/puddle_proof.py` does, and not read from the model?

items.statement: The wetness function gives the pores' fill and the surface water with its cover at a world point, from prepared fields and the rain state alone. It reads the stores by exposure, and is nothing under a roof; a wall takes a quarter of the ground's and an underside none; relief on a slope holds less, down to none at the class's steepest slope; where a class has a pattern, surface water covers its lows first. On the paving and the earth of part 5 of the design proof, ground that 0.4 of the rain reaches differs from that ground stepped by itself by no more than 0.3 of the pores and 0.15 mm of surface water.

A shrinking puddle leaves a damp margin whose height is the rate its level has lately fallen over the rate its ground dries, so a slow fall leaves a thin band and a fast one a wide band, and a rising puddle leaves none. Inside a body's wave support the pores are full, and above it they fall off over that body's margin as its stage falls. A margin and a shore's band add no water to the account.
items.ask: Does the shore's case read the wave support from `thrum-water-model`'s own function, so that it is the support `WATERS`' film reads?

items.statement: The wet look's reference darkens a base colour channel by channel by `(1 - R)(1 - p) a / (1 - p a)`, mixed in by the pores' fill times porosity: 0.55 of an albedo of 0.1 and 0.83 of 0.8 at `p` = 0.47, within 0.01; a brown's saturation rises; a metal is unchanged; a material with no porosity of its own takes the rule on roughness and metalness.

A drop's rings follow from water's dispersion with surface tension, depth and viscosity. The least group speed is 17.8 cm/s within 0.3. For a 3 mm drop over a crater three drop radii across, the rings' energy is the closed form's for a Gaussian impulse on deep water within 2%, and between 0.8% and 1.4% of the drop's; 0.8 s after, the highest ring is 0.14 mm within a fifth and the water within 11 cm of the drop's place stands under a tenth of that; and the height on 5 mm, 2 mm and 1 mm of water over the height on deep water is 0.76, 0.41 and 0.25 within 0.05.
items.ask: Does the test integrate the response itself, with its own Bessel function, and take the energy's closed form from its own algebra?

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the CPU: `thrum-water-model`'s surface model sums two rain bands through the one sum, with the depth limit and moments a wave layer has. The bands are a function of time: the same time gives the same field whatever was evaluated before. Scheduled rings over a patch follow the rain rate up to the profile's count, and the drops below the cut add their squared slope to the moments. The gain at a point is exposure times the depth response, on every body, the sea included, and none under a roof. With no rain bands every answer of the model is the same to the bit.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model --test rain_bands && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model
items.ask: Do the bands hold any state between evaluations, or any power that depends on the wind? Was any existing test of `thrum-water-model` changed?

items.statement: Ruling 2 is built on the CPU: the interaction reference takes a fine level with a ladder of 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 mm, the deep operator from 320 mm, and surface tension in its frequency. Over waves of 8 cm to 1 m on uniform depths from 5 mm to deep and midway between ladder depths, a step of one tick and of two has a phase speed within 3% of the true speed, never grows, and loses under 0.5% of a wave's height a second at one tick and under 3% at two. A frame more than two ticks ahead takes two steps and counts the rest as dropped. With a fine level the near level holds no wave under 1 m; with none, the reference's answers are the same to the bit.
items.check: cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model --test fine_level && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-water-model --test interaction
items.ask: Does the test show steps of eight ticks failing the loss, as part 6 of the design proof does? Were `WATERS`' interaction tests left as they were?

items.statement: On the fine level a footfall's rings cross 30 mm of water at the speed that depth gives within 5%, and slower on 10 mm. With two puddles a dry sill apart, a ring raised in one leaves the other exactly at rest. After the two merge, the same height and potential are still in the level, and a ring then crosses the drowned sill.

`WATERS`' conformance harness, run over a hollows body with rain bands and a fine level, reports nothing for the model against itself, and reports a provider that ignores exposure, by the points and the differences.

With it on the island has a yard by the lake, with paving that dips, a track of packed earth with ruts, a roof on posts, a wall and a post standing in a hollow, as a hollows body with its ground classes, and the game keeps a rain state in its world and steps it.

items.statement: Ruling 1 is built on the GPU. For a bed the test makes, at five fills that include the ticks before and after a merge, the body, level, bed and depth the GPU's map gives at 4,096 scattered points and along every puddle's waterline are `thrum-water-model`'s, within the bound `WATERS` M4.1 recorded. A scene with no hollows body compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before this milestone.
items.ask: Is a hollows body reached only through declarations any game can make, with no path in `thrum-water` that knows the island? Does the test fail when the GPU reads one level for the whole body?

items.statement: Each puddle is drawn level and whole. Seen from above, each pixel's water or ground is what the CPU model gives for that place, except within a cell of a waterline; the depth the water writes over each puddle is its level within M4.1's bound; and no triangle of the surface joins two levels over water.

A merge and a parting rebuild and reset nothing. Through both, the water creates no pipeline or resource, its history is marked invalid no more often than `WATERS`' reset rule gives, the body's identity and generation hold, and a float's query answers follow the level with no step.
A float released in a puddle sits at its level and rises as it fills; a query on the dry ground beside it and under the roof answers dry.

The puddles read as water lying in the ground: each level, meeting the paving and the earth in a clean line that follows the ground, with no stair of cells, no sliver on dry ground and no edge hanging in the air. The paving shows through its shallow puddles and the track's puddles are muddy and hide their bed. The sky lies in them. The film and the wet ground are not built until M5 and are not judged here.

milestones.name: Rain rings every water it falls on, the puddles, the lake and the sea, more and rougher as it grows and not at all under the roof, and a footfall in a puddle sends rings to its edges
milestones.quality_bar: Rain on water as on the lakes of Red Dead Redemption 2 and the street puddles of The Last of Us Part II, and past both in that each ring is the water's own wave: it starts small and sharp, spreads leaving calm water inside it, gains crests and fades, with no grid, repeat or stamped circle.

items.statement: Ruling 3 is built on the GPU. The two rain bands, evaluated at the display's time, differ from `thrum-water-model`'s at three times by no more than the bound this milestone first measures and records. A repeated frame at one time draws the same bands, and a capture at a tick draws that tick's. A scene without the capability compiles to the shader text, passes and storage it had before.
items.ask: Was the bound written from a measurement on this Mac, in the record with its date and commit? Do the bands keep any texture from one frame to the next?

items.statement: The bands' gain is the model's. Under the roof the drawn surface carries no ring and in the open it carries them; a ring on 2 mm of water is the depth response's share of one on a deep puddle; the lake and the sea carry them; the rings counted over a patch follow the rain at 2, 10 and 50 mm/h; and with no rain the bands' passes do not run.

A ring is water's own wave on the GPU: with one drop scheduled, the edge of the calm water inside its rings and its highest crest stand where the reference puts them 0.4 s and 0.8 s after, within the bound M4.1 recorded and a texel.

From 0.5 m and from 1.7 m the rings read as rain on water: each starts small and sharp, spreads leaving calm water inside it, gains crests and fades. Light rain is a few rings, heavy rain a crowded, roughened surface. No grid, repeat or pair of like rings shows across a puddle 6 m long. Under the roof's edge the rings stop along a soft line, and on the thinnest water they are faint.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences of the yard's largest puddle from 0.5 m and 1.7 m at 2, 10 and 50 mm/h, one framed on the roof's edge and one on a puddle's shallow margin; `fixed` stills cropped at native size of single rings at three ages.

items.ask: Is the visibility read through the lent operation `WATERS` M16 built, once for each direct-Sun term, with no shadow map sampled by the water itself? If `RIVERS` or `WATERS` had already built it for the surface, was only the film's added?

items.statement: Under reconstruction the rain's water holds up in motion: no shimmer in the rings near or far, no crawl along a waterline as a puddle grows, no ghost behind the marker or its rings, no swim in the film's reflections as the camera pans, and a clean reset on a cut.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences under TAAU on the Mac and in Chrome: a walk across the yard at 1.7 m in rain at 10 mm/h, a still camera on a filling puddle, a pan over wet paving at a grazing view, and a cut between two of them.

items.statement: From dawn to night the puddles and the wet ground are lit only by the engine's sky: at a waterline their light joins the ground's, wet paving glares toward a low Sun and nowhere else, and at night nothing glows.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the soaked yard at dawn, noon, sunset and night, toward the Sun and away from it, each whole and cropped at native size at a waterline and on the film.

items.statement: A water profile that leaves out hollows, rain bands, fine rings, wet ground or the standing film declares none of that capability's passes and creates none of its resources, and no shader makes its reads.
In Chrome the yard's puddles, rings, film and wet ground and the controls all run together from one command.

With everything this module adds in view the paired cost record is taken at 2560x1440 on tick frames and repeat frames, beside M5's, and the valley's again. Each tripwire tripped has its investigation beside it. No figure in either record decides this item.
